content.thinking:
I'm designing a koala clinging to a vertical eucalyptus branch mounted on a wood base plinth, with the koala standing on the ground plane and the branch leaning slightly for a natural grip pose.

Working out the coordinates now: positioning the branch pole to one side with its base and top points, placing the koala's body offset from it facing forward, and having one arm and leg reach across to grip the pole like the reference image shows.

Simpler to just have both arms reach the pole, with the right arm crossing in front of the chest and resting there, hand near the pole's front face, while the left hand grips higher up. Now I'm working out the overall body proportions for the sitting koala, placing the hips, spine curve, and head center to establish the scale.

Next I'm sizing the head and ears, then positioning the base plinth and pole geometry, with the pole running from near the base up to about 1.15m. I'm placing the rear feet gripping the pole low and laying out leg paths from hip to knee using simple curves to keep the rig manageable.

I'm checking that the foot positions sit flush against the pole's surface and simplifying by keeping the pole perfectly vertical instead of tilting it, since the body radius already touches the pole's base width. Now I'm moving into building the skeleton chain, starting with the hip root and planning the spine chain upward toward the chest and neck.

Building skeleton joints...

I'll sweep the chain from hips to chest with varying radii for body fullness, using round caps. I need to check the bottom of the body sits properly against the pole fork where the koala would actually rest.

For coloring, I'm defining a grey ramp for fur with countershading, a cream palette for the belly and chest bib based on normal and position thresholds, and adding dithering with random speckles for texture. For the head, I'm starting with a scaled sphere geometry as the base shape.

Now I'm adding muzzle and nose details — a cream-grey muzzle sphere, a dark rounded nose built from a scaled sphere with highlight pixels, and tiny textured eye boxes using pixel art decals placed on the head's surface.

Still working out eye placement geometrically on the curved head, calculating the sphere surface offset so the eyes sit flush against the head at the right depth, then simplifying to small dark spheres with white glint spheres for a robust, easy approach.

I'm now adding a cream muzzle patch scaled flatter under the nose, positioning the nose on top, and setting up a separate jaw piece parented to the head with a mouth line for detail.

For the ears, I'm shaping fluffy outer fur spheres positioned at the sides of the head angled outward, each with an inner pink disc shape slightly offset to face forward.

Placing tuft cards in a ring around the ear center with an outward-facing frame, defaulting to standard card flow and double-sided pixel fur texture. I'm also considering scattering a small number of fur tuft cards across the body surface for added texture, though that risks looking too busy.

Now I'm working out the arm joint chains for both sides—shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions—so I can build a catmull-rom spline through named bone points for a reaching-up pose.

Working out the finger wrap geometry...

I'm checking that the elbow position lands on the chest surface and that shoulder joints sit within the body radius, adjusting arm thickness to taper slightly. Now I'm laying out the leg joints—hip, knee, foot—for a squatting stance, naming them and starting on their radii.

For toes I'll reuse the grip function with four smaller digits. Then I'm sweeping the pole as a slightly curved rod using a catmull spline with tapering radius, and painting bark texture with vertical brown grain stripes via a procedural cell paint ramp.

Writing bark hash function...

I'll add a pale cut disk at the top with a ring texture to show the sawed cross-section, oriented along the branch tangent. Now moving to the eucalyptus leaves -- planning lance-shaped sprigs with extruded outlines, a central vein, and green paint coloring.

For the vein effect, I'm checking pixel-level coordinates so a lighter yellowgreen streak appears near the leaf's centerline. Then I'm attaching clusters of leaves to stems that sweep outward from the pole, figuring out leaf orientation based on the stem tip direction.

Working through the leaf orientation math, I want the hanging leaves to show some thickness and face sideways rather than lying edge-on, so I'm setting up the y-axis as a sideways vector derived from crossing the stem direction with an upward vector, which should give a more natural draping look.

Writing eucalyptus sprig geometry...

For the plinth, I'm planning a wooden base stand with a pixel plank texture, maybe an octagonal lathe-style disc using a cylinder geometry sized around 0.28 radius and 0.07 height.

Now I'm stacking two stepped disc layers for the base, positioning the pole bottom to sink into it, adding a dark brass collar ring around the pole's lower section, and scattering tiny screw boxes along the base's top rim for detail.

Working out the apothem distance so the plaque sits flush against the flat face, placing it slightly offset in z and y—though a full pixel-font text render feels too heavy, so I'm leaning toward a simpler drawn label instead.

Working out plaque sizing...

I'm stacking the second cylindrical step above the base, adjusting heights so each tier sits flush, then placing the pole and feet accordingly. I'm also scattering a few fallen leaves flat on the base top for detail, and now moving on to koala features like nose, claws, and toes.

For the koala's coloring I'm planning the cream chin and belly bib against the grey back, plus ear fur texture and padded feet, while keeping the finger rigging simple without extra digit joints to avoid overcomplicating the skeleton. I'm defining the body as a pear-shaped sweep along the spine chain with radii tapering from the hips, giving it a bottom-heavy koala silhouette with rounded caps at each end.

Writing fur paint logic...

Writing fur paint logic...

Planning the hand grip geometry now, computing finger joint positions with angle-based polar coordinates around a central pole radius, dipping each knuckle slightly along y.

Setting the arm path endpoint at the wrist, with the palm as a small grey sphere there, and giving feet bigger four-toe grippers with wider spacing than the hands. Checking body proportions, I'm placing shoulders relative to chest radius and routing the elbow forward before the wrist along the arm's catmull path.

Working out the mirrored right arm joints similarly, then the leg chains -- hips to knees to feet, keeping hip joints tucked inside the body and knees pushed forward for a slight squat stance. I'm setting up the parenting hierarchy so legs attach to hips and arms attach to the chest/spine joint, making sure the chain's starting positions match their parent joints exactly.

Now I'm adding the head, jaw, and ear joints -- placing the head centered above the chest, the jaw slightly below and forward, and symmetric ears on either side with hinge roles, sizing their spheres and tilting them outward so they don't overlap too badly with the head.

Working out the Y-rotation sign so the ear's normal vector properly faces outward for both left and right sides, then moving to position the inner pink ear detail offset along the radius.

Checking it extends slightly beyond the outer ear but stays within bounds, so that's fine. Now I'm working out the tuft ring of cards around the ear, placing them in a plane perpendicular to the normal using the bone frame, sizing and leaning each card so they follow the ear's curvature with the flow direction aligned to the surface normal.

I'm designing the pixel-art fur tuft texture as a small grid, with grey forming the root at the bottom and white fur above it, then planning to reuse a similar grey palette for scattering fur cards across the body.

Scattering body fur cards using a filtered surface sweep, biased toward the lower half with controlled density, lean angle, and size. I'm also adding smaller white cheek tufts on the head using a normal-direction filter to target the lower sides of the face, and sketching out a small dark rod for the mouth.

I'm positioning the nose as a wide dark trapezoid-shaped sphere scaled flatter on the muzzle, with a subtle grey highlight sphere on top for texture, and considering a lighter grey patch for nostril shading instead of separate dark nostril holes.

Now I'm working out the muzzle sphere position and size so it reaches the correct front depth, then calculating eye placement coordinates relative to the head's offset center, being careful about which direction is the model's left versus the mirrored side.

Adding a dark fur ring behind the eye, then setting up static body parts bound to bones while keeping the color palette modest and under the 64-color limit. I'm starting the import statements and metadata scaffolding for the character builder script.

Now I'm working out a seeded hash function for deterministic randomness, then building a bark paint function that blends several brown tones using cell-based noise to create peeling patches of lighter color near the surface.

Then I'm setting up the leaf paint logic—picking from a palette of greens with a lighter vein color drawn along the cell's central axis, modulated with noise to vary shading across the leaf surface.

Now I'm defining a leaf-generation function that computes orientation vectors from direction and roll, then builds a tapered outline using a width profile based on a sine curve, sampling points along the leaf's length to form its characteristic shape.

Marking the origin as not sharp while the last point stays sharp, I'm writing the extrude call for the leaves with thickness, smoothing, and color set, then figuring out which bone they should ride on. Since leaves and other static elements like the pole and plinth don't move, I'll attach them all to the hips joint as the common root bone.

For the sprigs, I'm defining a function that places a base point on the pole and computes an outward direction using angle and rise, then builds a small stem path with a catmull-rom sweep tapering from thicker to thinner, colored brown-green, with leaves branching off at a few points along the stem.

Still writing sprig leaf placement...

Checking the ear positions against the pole again, I'm finding the right ear overlaps slightly in z-range, so I'm nudging its center outward in both x and z to clear the pole's bounding box.

Still refining pole position function...

Writing fur sweep parameters...

Checking that head scaling and positioning overlaps correctly with the chest and neck, then moving to the wood baseboard paint pattern using a ring-based procedural texture.

Now I'm adding screws around the base, placing eight small cylinders ringed near the top step, then setting up a few fallen leaf shapes lying flat and slightly sunken into the base surface.

Checking overall proportions: the base sits flush with the floor, and the total model is roughly 0.6 wide by 1.3 tall. I'm also shaping the jaw and muzzle with scaled spheres in cream tones, then moving on to set up the ear joints.

Finalizing the typed structures: frames for cards, bone references for joints, and the noise and paint functions returning proper color types. For the plaque, I'm drawing a background fill, stamping letter rows within the available space, and adding a gold underline near the bottom edge.

Figuring out letter spacing so the glyphs fit evenly across the 23-pixel width, then placing the plaque as a plane geometry on the hips bone, oriented to face forward along the +z axis so it's visible from the front. Now I'm starting on the body fur texture using a tufted grey pattern.

Adding the cream bib paint condition using positional checks, then writing out the full file.
